title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Daily batch, 23 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred, relevance-ranked selection rather than a popularity ranking. Biomedical arXiv coverage is incomplete relative to bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the wider medical literature. The listed computational, in-vitro, and imaging findings are not clinical practice-changing evidence.

sections.title: Daily biology and biomedicine batch — 23 October 2026
sections.summary: Ten notable papers; RNA design is prominent, alongside single-cell privacy methods and mechanistic biomolecular models. Ranking is inferred from relevance and reported study design, not measured popularity.

sections.title: ProMORNA: An End-to-End Generative Framework for Full-Length mRNA Design
sections.abstract: Protein-conditioned encoder–decoder generation of full-length mRNAs with multi-objective post-training; the authors report in-silico gains and increased Fluc2P reporter activity for selected candidates across three independent in-vitro experiments.
sections.claimed_contribution: Candidate 2 had 3.33× the conventional benchmark's 12–72 h reporter-activity AUC (Holm-adjusted P=0.01285); its 1.29× estimate versus the selected GEMORNA candidate remained exploratory after correction.
sections.unique_caveat: Fluc2P in-vitro reporter evidence does not establish therapeutic efficacy, in-vivo performance, or generalization across payloads; the GEMORNA comparison was not significant after correction.

sections.title: RiboBridge: protein-conditioned de novo RNA binder structure design
sections.abstract: RiboBridge separates RNA conformation generation from protein-relative assembly to produce candidate protein–RNA structures without a specified binding site.
sections.claimed_contribution: On a temporally split, sequence-filtered benchmark of 124 protein–RNA complexes, authors report top fNAT and DockQ and lowest interface/ligand RMSDs under post-hoc interface-correspondence evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: Native interface information is used after generation to choose the corresponding predicted-pocket candidate; structure recovery is not evidence of binding or biological activity.

sections.title: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
sections.abstract: The authors benchmark scGFT, scLDM, and Cell2Sentence for single-cell RNA-seq utility and membership-inference privacy, finding that non-HVG reconstruction choices affect privacy leakage.
sections.claimed_contribution: The donor split contains 633,711 training cells from 490 donors and 634,022 test cells from 491 donors; Poisson reconstruction of non-HVG values reduces leakage in tested settings.
sections.unique_caveat: Generation focused mainly on highly variable genes because of compute constraints; this is one dataset and does not establish privacy across attacks or populations.

sections.title: Supercoiling Drives DNA-Protein Co-Condensation
sections.abstract: A coupled DNA-elasticity/protein-field model predicts that DNA supercoiling and protein wetting reinforce each other and can facilitate co-condensation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' theoretical model predicts twist-to-writhe conversion, capillary collapse, and a lowered modeled nucleation barrier under sufficient supercoiling.
sections.unique_caveat: Theory and simulation only; the model uses an idealized closed DNA loop and simplified DNA–protein/solvent interactions.

sections.title: Escaping the Phylogenetic Trap: Persistent Homology Enables Cross-Species Ion Channel Classification via Multimodal Graph Neural Networks
sections.abstract: A sequence-and-structure classifier uses persistent-homology features to improve venom-compound ion-channel target classification when entire taxa are held out.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports 63.4% leave-one-taxon-out accuracy on 1,373 predicted venom compounds across five taxa, over eight percentage points above the next-best tested method.
sections.unique_caveat: Structures are ColabFold predictions and classification metrics do not demonstrate experimentally validated toxin binding or channel effects.

sections.title: Shorter but not more catalytic: an active-site-resolved model of how tau reshapes amyloid-β secondary nucleation
sections.abstract: An active-site-resolved kinetic model examines how tau cross-seeding affects amyloid-β42 fibrils and secondary nucleation, finding that shorter fibrils alone need not be more catalytic.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 800 Latin-hypercube samples, the model predicts catalytic effects depend on active-site number/activity/exposure and the balance of monomer clearance and elongation.
sections.unique_caveat: Model-dependent mechanistic predictions, not new aggregation measurements or patient outcomes.

sections.title: Behavioral Mapping of Hierarchical Dynamical Models Accelerates Bayesian Parameter Inference
sections.abstract: Posterior information from a simpler model is used to screen proposals for a more detailed model, tested on gene-expression models fitted to cell-free data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 8.02% and 15.21% MCMC speedups for phenomenological and mechanistic models after initial setup costs.
sections.unique_caveat: Tested on one gene-expression model hierarchy and cell-free data; reported gains may not transfer to other models.

sections.title: Direct Production of Ultra-High Radioisotopic Pure ⁶⁴Cu from Natural Zinc Metal via D-D Fusion Narrowband Fast Neutron Source Irradiation
sections.abstract: Natural zinc irradiated by a D-D fusion neutron source yielded no-carrier-added ⁶⁴Cu with high measured radioisotopic purity, suggesting an alternative isotope-production route.
sections.claimed_contribution: After one-hour irradiation and 72-hour gamma spectroscopy, the authors report 99.62% minimum and 99.97% threshold-corrected ⁶⁴Cu radioisotopic purity.
sections.unique_caveat: A single irradiation protocol does not demonstrate routine scale-up, cost in manufacturing, clinical availability, or patient benefit.

sections.title: AI Enhanced Cerenkov Luminescence Microscopy
sections.abstract: A Monte-Carlo-guided CARE network restores simulated Cerenkov microscopy images and is applied to experimental images of 27 ¹⁸F-FDG-treated U87 tumor spheroids.
sections.claimed_contribution: On synthetic validation data, the authors report MSE 0.0051 versus 0.0492 for Noise2Void and improved localization/contrast metrics on experimental spheroid images.
sections.unique_caveat: Quantitative ground truth is simulated and experimental application is limited to a small U87 spheroid set, not patient or clinical validation.

sections.title: Geometry-Dependent Properties of Physically Crosslinked PPy-PVA Hydrogels Enable Tunable Iontophoretic Drug Delivery
sections.abstract: Five PPy-PVA hydrogel geometries carrying bovine serum albumin were compared for iontophoretic transport using finite-element modeling and Franz diffusion cells with artificial membranes.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report geometry-dependent transport and mean iontophoretic permeability of (3.80 ± 1.93) × 10⁻⁵ in their artificial-membrane assay.
sections.unique_caveat: BSA and artificial-membrane results do not establish transport through intact human skin or clinical delivery.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: RNA design (ProMORNA, RiboBridge); privacy-aware single-cell and out-of-distribution evaluation (OneK1K benchmark, ion-channel classifier); mechanistic models of biomolecular state (DNA co-condensation, tau/amyloid). Several separate medical-physics proofs of concept appear, without evidence of one unified clinical trend.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Test protein–RNA binders for binding and function; assess mRNA design beyond Fluc2P; evaluate synthetic-data privacy on external donors and attacks; experimentally vary DNA topology/protein affinity; extend image-restoration, hydrogel, and isotope-production validation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The fresh-batch signal is topical, not statistical: RNA design, single-cell privacy, and mechanistic biomolecular models stand out; the experimental results remain early and bounded.
